context: The agent must commit a single-file Python bug fix to a project that has a Makefile with a 'checks' target. The scenario tests whether the agent runs pre-commit checks via 'make checks' and writes a properly-formatted conventional commit message (correct type, imperative mood, lower case, no trailing period, under 60 characters, no emoji, no unnecessary body).

checklist.name: Ran make checks
checklist.description: workflow.md contains evidence that 'make checks' was run before committing (e.g. output line 'checks passed' or the command itself)

checklist.name: Checks passed before commit
checklist.description: workflow.md shows the pre-commit check completed without errors (not skipped, not failed silently)

checklist.name: Correct commit type
checklist.description: The commit message subject starts with 'fix' (not feat, chore, refactor, or any other type)

checklist.name: Imperative mood subject
checklist.description: The commit subject verb is in imperative mood (e.g. 'fix', 'guard', 'prevent', 'handle') rather than past tense ('fixed', 'added') or gerund ('fixing')

checklist.name: Lower case subject
checklist.description: The commit subject (after the type prefix) begins with a lower-case letter

checklist.name: No trailing period
checklist.description: The commit subject line does NOT end with a period

checklist.name: Subject under 60 characters
checklist.description: The full commit subject line (type + colon + subject) is fewer than 60 characters

checklist.name: No emoji in commit message
checklist.description: The commit message (subject and body if present) contains no emoji characters

checklist.name: Subject-line-only commit
checklist.description: The commit message has no body — it is a subject line alone (no extra paragraphs or bullets after the subject)
